gap: No result ChatGPT got states that regenerative braking is a charge into the pack, so a LiFePO4 battery whose BMS blocks charging below 32°F also blocks regen current. Eco Battery says in its own FAQ that 'Carts with regenerative charging may encounter issues below this temperature.' Vatrer's own page describes its heated 48V 105Ah pack as warming from 'charging input', which means plugged-in charging, not driving.
standout_why: I read three pages. golfcartshowdown.com (cited) has BMS amp ratings and charger warnings but no mention of regen, OBC or controller matching. golfcartlab.com (cited) explains BMS continuous current against a 400A controller and covers heated versus unheated packs, with nothing on regen. golfcartbatterysource.com's buyer's guide (cited in the second chat) has both halves, but on separate lines. It says the EZGO RXV and AC-drive carts 'push current back into the pack' and that most packs 'will not charge below about 32°F unless they have a built-in heater'. It never links the two, never quotes a maker on it, and never says whether a heater works while the cart is driving. Because that page has the parts separately, this scores 2 rather than 3.
decides: This matters only for shoppers with a regen cart (EZGO RXV, AC-drive carts) who park or drive below freezing. For them, a pack with a 32°F charge cutoff and no heater cannot take regen current on a cold morning. That covers LiTime 48V 100Ah and Vatrer's standard 105Ah kits, which are ChatGPT's budget and value picks. The fix is a self-heating pack. Even then, Vatrer's heated model warms from charger input, so it fixes charging but has no sourced effect on regen while driving. Eco Battery's Gen3 auto-heating packs are the only ones whose maker says they 'can safely charge at temperatures below 32°F'. That supports ChatGPT's premium Eco pick for cold-climate regen carts. For DC series-drive carts without regen (EZGO TXT, Club Car DS), this finding doesn't affect the choice, and the 200A-BMS budget packs stay fine.
